title: Harden operator federation (RFC 9421, replies)
description: 06-operators, 07-reply-protocol. Use RFC 9421 created/expires, drop corundum-timestamp; alg name ed25519 not ed25519-v1 in 9421 params; replay: require idempotent POSTs keyed by content CID (nonce only if needed); bind keyid origin to submittingOperator/manifest id; rate-limit refetch-on-failure; revocation lags up to 24h cache; auth.required inbound/outbound ambiguity; add insufficient-signature-coverage to code list; Content-Digest is RFC 9530; remove 'faster than TLS' claim. Trust levels: define wire strings or drop requireMinimumTrustLevel; 'known' via untrusted directory. Reply validation: require inReplyTo==parentId and signer==author; mutuals-only isn't mutual; followers-only fails closed on lost notification; 'held for retry' has no response code; state that the reply tree, not inReplyTo, defines threads; parent-migrated code.
notes:
From esol.10: 07:207 (Ch 23) still says BLOCKED_USER -> REPLY_REJECTED/blocked-user; batch reply endpoint has no response format; no reason code for future-dated published (TIMESTAMP_SKEW?).
From esol.4: Operator Manifest self-signature -> attached JWS (Ch 34), corundumType OperatorManifest, kid = manifest key id. keys[].algorithm values -> JOSE alg names ('Ed25519'). RFC 9421 alg param uses 9421 registry name 'ed25519'. Ch 21: replace reply.signingRecord schema with detached JWS SigningRecord (Ch 12); drop reply.contentHash (CID covers it); require activity bytes inline or fetched by id. From esol.3: attributedTo/parentAuthor/ipns:// refs in 07 -> DIDs.
From esol.3: 07:188 requireVerifiedIdentity: every user now has a DID; redefine as 'DID method with recovery (not did:key)' or drop. Ch 17/18 operators no longer hold user update keys; content key operator-held by default.
From esol.11: Ch 19 example still alg="ed25519-v1".
From esol.5: 07:176 per-post replyPolicy cannot live on the (now immutable, minimal) Entry; move to a signed activity field (e.g. replyPolicy in the activity, changed only by edit). 07:54/84/86 reply trees are now located via the operator-published ReplyMap (Ch 10, IPNS name owned by operator); hostile migration: new operator copies old ReplyMap from IPFS. Ch 21 must accept edited replies as fresh submissions (Ch 13).
